headline: Highest-quality franchise with strong momentum, but the market already pays for it and fuel forced a large 2026 guidance cut.
business: Delta flies from Atlanta, Detroit, Minneapolis, Salt Lake City, New York and other hubs, and earns the industry's richest premium and co-brand card revenue (American Express). Largest market cap in the group at $54.9B.
recent: Q3 2026 operating revenue $20.2B (+21.1%); net income $756M ($1.15/share, -47%); adjusted EPS $1.72 vs $1.70; adjusted operating margin 9.4% vs 11.1%.
Cut 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50, citing a ~$6B fuel cost increase; Q4 adjusted EPS guided to $1.15-$1.65.
Adjusted Q3 earnings of ~$1.13B topped United's $833M on lower adjusted revenue, underlining Delta's cost and premium-mix edge.
strengths: Strongest brand and premium/loyalty economics in the industry
+44% 1-year return, near the top of the group
Only network carrier paying a dividend
risks: Thin cash ($3.8B, 5% of revenue), the lowest liquidity ratio of the peers
Priciest forward P/E among profitable majors (11.4x)
